lesson_title: The Rule of the Nizams: Hyderabad's Journey

scenes.purpose: Introduce the main topic: the rule of the Nizams of Hyderabad.
scenes.teacher_script: Hello, young historians! Today, we're embarking on an exciting journey to explore the fascinating rule of the Nizams in Hyderabad. Let's uncover their story!

scenes.purpose: Explain the origin and founder of the Asaf Jahi dynasty.
scenes.teacher_script: After the Mughal Empire weakened, its governors asserted independence. One powerful figure, Chin Qulich Khan, also known as Nizam-Ul-Mulk, founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty in Hyderabad in 1724.

template_data.title: Birth of the Asaf Jahi Dynasty

scenes.purpose: Provide an overview of the Asaf Jahi rulers and who received the 'Nizam' title.
scenes.teacher_script: The Asaf Jahi dynasty saw ten rulers from 1724 to 1948. Interestingly, only seven of them actually received the prestigious title 'Nizam' from the Mughals.

rows: Nazar Jung, Muzafar Jung, Sabath Jung

scenes.purpose: Explain the reasons behind the Nizams' growing dependency on the British.
scenes.teacher_script: The Nizams constantly fought the Marathas and Mysore rulers to create their independent state. However, these continuous wars made them reliant on the British, eventually leading to a loss of their full independent status.

bullets: Aimed to carve independent Hyderabad State

scenes.purpose: Illustrate Hyderabad's development under British influence and 'colonial modernisation'.
scenes.teacher_script: Under the influence of British officials, the Nizams adopted 'colonial modernization'. The British were fond of Hyderabad's unique culture, and this period saw significant development in the late 19th century.

scenes.purpose: Highlight key figures and their contributions to reforms and development.
scenes.teacher_script: Salar Jung, a prominent Prime Minister from 1853 to 1883, championed colonial development schemes. The Sixth Nizam, Mir Mahabub Ali Khan, also marked his period with numerous reforms, including building significant institutions.

attributes.label: Salar Jung I (PM)
attributes.value:
• Prime Minister (1853-1883)
• Imbibed colonial development schemes

attributes.label: Mir Mahabub Ali Khan
attributes.value:
• Sixth Nizam
• Period marked with many reforms
• Founded Asafia Library, Victoria Memorial Orphanage, Mahabubia Girls School

scenes.purpose: Describe the VII Nizam's stance on feudal power despite reform movements.
scenes.teacher_script: Towards the later period, the Seventh Nizam, despite popular movements for liberal reforms, was determined to protect the existing feudal power structure.

attributes.label: Nizam's Stance
attributes.value: Determined to protect feudal power structure

scenes.purpose: Test the student's understanding of the key concepts learned.
scenes.teacher_script: Fantastic! You've learned so much about the Nizams. Let's test your knowledge with a quick question before we conclude!

template_data.question: Who founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty of Hyderabad State?
template_data.explanation: Chin Qulich Khan, known as Nizam-Ul-Mulk, founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty in 1724 after the weakening of the Mughal Empire.
